label: EU(7)-PIM: theophylline
title: Theophylline in an older person
statement: Theophylline is on the EU(7)-PIM list of medicines to avoid in older people, because it has a higher risk of stimulant effects on the brain and nervous system. For a new start, the list suggests a dose 25% below the younger adult dose and a starting maximum of 400 mg/day. It also suggests checking theophylline blood levels to guide dose adjustment.

plain_summary: Theophylline can overstimulate the nervous system in an older person, so its use and dose need a regular review and blood level checks.

medicine_groups.name: Theophylline
medicine_groups.note: Tablets, slow-release tablets and liquids taken by mouth count. Aminophylline is a related medicine that the source row does not name, so it is not counted here. Roflumilast is a different medicine and does not count.

rule_for_models: In a person aged 65 years or older, flag one or more supplies of oral theophylline. If age is missing and the supply otherwise qualifies, report only a possible finding and ask the pharmacist to confirm whether the person is 65 or older. A recorded age below 65 gives no finding. Mention a starting dose above 400 mg/day only when the record documents a new start and the strength and directions establish a daily dose above that figure.
cannot_be_seen: A supply alone cannot establish when treatment began or how the person takes the medicine. A theophylline level, smoking status or interacting medicine supply can be seen when recorded. Other pharmacy supplies and unrecorded changes in smoking or medicine use can be missed.
ask_the_gp: Whether theophylline is still needed, whether the dose is suitable, and when the last blood level of theophylline was checked.
